title: Input rows for one data-driven Arazzo workflow
description: Sits beside the Arazzo document whose workflow it feeds, named `<workflowId>.rows.yaml`; `workflow` repeats that workflow's case id. Each row binds the workflow's `inputs` by property name: a key the inputs schema does not name is refused, every `required` input is bound in every row, and each row validates against the inputs schema. An input of `format: uuid` with no value is generated per row. A value under a column `literals` names is a decision-table literal, and `validate` refuses one that does not parse against the literal grammar, naming its row, its column and the character offset of the production that fails. A `recipe` binds one or two more inputs per row from the row's literals, and the row it completes is what the inputs schema validates. A file with `server` may omit `rows`: the workflow then runs once, with only its generated and declared inputs, and `validate` refuses a file whose workflow requires any other input. A workflow that declares no inputs takes such a file and no rows.

workflow.description: The case id of the workflow, `<document>/<workflowId>`.

iteration.description: `reset_per_row` runs each row against fresh preconditions; `single_pass` runs every row against one shared server state.

literals.description: The columns whose values are decision-table literals: a range `a..b`, a list `[x, y]`, a unit-scoped range `cm 5.0..10.0`, a terminology code `openehr::122 (length)`, an ordinal tuple `1|[local::at0005]`, a quantity `100 mg`, or a plain scalar. Each names an input the workflow declares.

recipe.description: The registered recipe that turns each row's literals into the values of more inputs. `content_instance` builds the composition a content decision-table row commits: the `rm_class` value from the literal columns, in the minimal carrier composition stamped with `template_id`. `content_synthesized` serves a table whose rows vary the template: per row it builds the operational template (OPT 1.4 XML text) from the literal columns, under the id `template_id` followed by a digest of the template the row's constraint columns build, binds it to `template_input`, and binds the composition stamped with that id to `input`.

input.description: The workflow input the recipe binds; no row supplies it.

template_id.description: The template family: each row's template id is this id, a dot and eight hex digits.

input.description: The workflow input the composition is bound to; no row supplies it.

template_input.description: The workflow input the row's operational template is bound to; no row supplies it.

server.description: What the workflow needs the server under test to be. `exclusive`: the workflow changes state it did not create, such as a delete of every EHR, so it runs only when the party's IXIT declares `environment.exclusive_server: true`; any other IXIT skips every row with the reason `not-declared`.

declared.description: Inputs bound from a value the party declares: each maps an input the workflow declares to `ixit.<member>…` or `statement.<member>…`, a dotted path into the party's IXIT or statement. No row supplies a declared input. A run whose party does not declare the value skips every row with the reason `not-declared`.

aggregate.description: Properties of the whole run, judged once after the last row and only under `single_pass`. `distinct` names a workflow output no two rows may share; each entry carries the citation that assigns the property.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The citation, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.
